1.q: What is the main purpose of warning signs near public barriers?
o: To advertise the contractor's name.
To decorate and brighten the fencing.
To warn people of hazards and show directions.

n.0: Advertising is not the safety purpose.

n.3: Supervision and other controls may still be needed.
n.4: Signs support but do not replace physical controls.

1.q: What should be done with cylinder valves when cylinders are not in use?
o: Close the valves and fit any guards
Leave the valves cracked open slightly
Tap the valves to loosen them
Leave the valves fully open
Paint over the valve threads

n.3: Fully open valves allow gas to leak out.
n.4: Painting the threads is not a suitable measure.

1.q: You are outside after evacuating. What should you do next?
o: Drive off home without telling anyone
Go back inside for your work tools
Leave the site straight away for home

1.w: Remain at the assembly point so you can be accounted for and receive instructions.

n.0: Leaving without reporting may delay confirmation you are safe.
n.1: Do not re-enter until authorised.
n.2: Leaving may cause confusion during roll call.
n.3: Entrances should remain clear for emergency services.

1.q: A grinder guard has been removed because it makes cutting faster. What is the best action?
o: Ask another worker to use it instead

Do not use it and report it at once

Wear extra gloves and carry on

n.0: Passing the risk to others is unacceptable.
n.1: Speed does not justify unsafe use.
n.3: Small tasks still carry serious risk.
n.4: Gloves do not replace machine guarding.

1.q: Why are emergency drills carried out on site?
o: To avoid the site inductions
To practise for safer, faster response
To replace all the supervision
To test who is the fastest runner

n.0: Inductions are still required.
n.2: Supervision remains necessary.
n.3: Speed alone is not the aim.
n.4: They have a genuine safety purpose.

1.q: Which sequence is best after discovering a fire and reaching a call point?
o: Gather your tools, then raise the alarm, then leave
Fight the fire first, then raise the alarm, then leave
Leave the site, then let someone know about it later
Phone a friend for advice, then decide what to do next
Raise the alarm, leave by a safe exit, go to the assembly point
1.w: Raise the alarm promptly, evacuate safely, then report to assembly point.

n.0: Do not delay raising the alarm to collect tools.
n.1: Warning others comes before any optional fire-fighting.
n.2: Others need to be warned immediately, not later.
n.3: A personal call is not part of the emergency response.

1.q: If a transformer is making unusual noises or smells hot, what should you do?
o: Carry on until the task is complete
Cover it over with a coat

Move it nearer to the wall

n.0: Continuing with suspect equipment is unsafe.
n.1: Covering it may make overheating worse.
n.2: Kicking electrical equipment is dangerous.

1.q: What should be included in a quick load assessment before lifting?

n.1: Speed is not what the assessment is about.
n.2: Distance alone is not enough to plan the lift.
n.3: Being watched has nothing to do with safe handling.

1.q: Which situation most clearly shows a mask may have failed?

1.q: You need to enter a trench that has vertical sides and no support system fitted. What should you do?
